oligos.indication: research reagent - physiological knockdown of Galpha-i2 in rat ependyma
oligos.design_source: Monkkonen 2007 BMC Neurosci 8:26, PMID 17430589, DOI 10.1186/1471-2202-8-26, Methods 'Oligonucleotides'
oligos.notes: CRITICAL CHEMISTRY QUALIFIER: this is an UNMODIFIED phosphodiester DNA 18-mer, not a phosphorothioate and not a 2'-modified gapmer. The Methods say 'unmodified 18-mer oligonucleotides' and that 'RNase free, aseptic conditions were maintained until implantation of the cannulas to prevent degradation of unmodified oligonucleotides'. ps_count=0 and backbone_chemistry=full_PO follow directly from that statement. Targets nucleotides 150-167 (N-terminal coding region) of rat Galpha-i2; the authors state the sequence matched no other rat sequence. HPLC-purified, 90-97% purity, dissolved in sterile saline. Sequence transcribed verbatim from the Methods (printed there as 5'-CTT GTC GAT CAT CTT AGA-3'); the source printed it in flat upper case with no chemistry-encoding case, and it is stored that way per the schema's sequence-case rule.

oligos.indication: research reagent - sequence-specificity control for the anti-Galpha-i2 AS-ODN
oligos.notes: THE CHEMISTRY CONTROL THAT DECIDES THE MECHANISM QUESTION. Same unmodified phosphodiester DNA chemistry, same length, same route, same dose and same base composition as the anti-Galpha-i2 AS-ODN, differing only by eight mismatches; the Methods call it 'a more stringent control, maintaining equal base composition to the antisense molecule but with eight mismatches', and state it matched no rat sequence. Because this molecule produced NO ventricular dilatation in vivo and NO change in ciliary beat frequency in vitro at identical exposure, the AS-ODN effect is attributable to knockdown of the TARGET (Galpha-i2), not to oligonucleotide chemistry. Sequence transcribed verbatim from the Methods, printed there as 5'-TCTGCTGATACTCTTGAA-3' with the eight mismatched positions set off typographically in the original.

oligos.indication: research reagent - non-targeting control for the anti-Galpha-i2 AS-ODN
oligos.notes: Second, non-base-matched control ODN; same unmodified phosphodiester DNA chemistry, length, route and dose as the AS-ODN. The Methods state the nonsense sequence matched no rat sequence. Used as the ODN control arm in the histology and Galpha-i2 immunohistochemistry figures (Fig 5, Fig 7), where the ependymal cell layer was normal. Sequence transcribed verbatim from the Methods, printed there as 5'-GGG GGA AGT AGG TCT TGG-3'. Note the run of five consecutive G residues: a G-quartet motif is itself a known source of sequence-specific non-antisense effects, which is a reason the base-composition-matched mismatch ODN (TMP_hb_6) is the stronger control of the two.

measurements.effect_vs_control: significantly increased vs contralateral, 3rd and 4th ventricles and vs saline and mismatch-ODN control groups; p < 0.001 from day 2; plateau on day 4
measurements.source_table: Figure 1 (ventricular volumes in uL and wall surface areas in mm2 by Cavalieri principle from serial high-resolution MRI) and Results, 'Magnetic Resonance Imaging reveals the time-course for ventricular dilatation'
measurements.notes: THE ONE MECHANISTIC ANIMAL SOURCE THAT EXISTS FOR OLIGONUCLEOTIDE-ASSOCIATED VENTRICULAR DILATATION. Continuous ICV infusion of an antisense ODN against Galpha-i2 produced UNILATERAL ventricular dilatation confined to the infused ventricle. readout_value=TBD because the uL values exist only as plotted points in Figure 1 and are not stated numerically in the text - inventing a number here would be fabrication. GRADE RATIONALE: grade 2 ('ventriculomegaly without clinical decompensation') rather than 3, because the animals grew normally (Fig 2, no significant group difference), showed no gross behavioural abnormality on motor coordination, anxiety, motor activity, pain perception or morphine analgesia testing, and required no intervention; the only clinical sign was dehydration from day 2. Grade 3 was considered because the dilatation was irreversible and accompanied by destruction of the ependymal layer (see TMP_hb_m21) - a reviewer may wish to harmonise this row upward with that one. The authors explicitly decline to call it hydrocephalus: 'Since the intracranial pressure was not assessed in this study, we call the condition ventricular dilatation instead of hydrocephalus in this text.' Dosing: continuous ICV infusion into the RIGHT lateral ventricle via Alzet minipump (models 1007D/2002) at 25 ug/day for 7 days, started at surgery on postnatal day 24 in young Wistar rats (3-5 weeks, 50-100 g); the same procedure in adult rats (250 g, n=5) reproduced the finding. dose_or_conc_value=25 with unit ug is the DAILY dose; the infusion schedule is carried in exposure_duration because the vocabulary has no ug/day unit. MECHANISM VERDICT - TARGET-DRIVEN, NOT CHEMISTRY-DRIVEN. The paper carries three concurrent control arms at identical route and dose (saline n=22, nonsense ODN n=17, mismatch ODN n=5, vs antisense n=27), of which the mismatch ODN is base-composition-matched to the antisense with eight mismatches. Neither control ODN produced ventricular dilatation in vivo or any change in ciliary beat frequency in vitro, while Galpha-i2 protein knockdown in ependymal cells was independently confirmed by immunohistochemistry with two antibodies. The effect is therefore pharmacology specific to loss of Galpha-i2, not a property of oligonucleotide chemistry. GENERALISATION LIMIT, EQUALLY IMPORTANT: the molecule is an UNMODIFIED PHOSPHODIESTER DNA 18-mer with zero phosphorothioate linkages and no 2' modification, i.e. it shares essentially no chemistry with nusinersen, tofersen or tominersen. This row therefore supports the claim 'knocking down Galpha-i2 causes ventricular dilatation in rats' and does NOT support 'intrathecal ASOs cause hydrocephalus'. grade_provisional.

3. THE MONKKONEN PAPER IS REAL AND WAS FOUND AND READ IN FULL.

   ciliary stasis and ventricular dilatation in the rat." BMC Neurosci 2007 Apr 12;8:26.

   cc_by. Fetched: EuropePMC full text XML of PMC1855344.
   The brief's description is accurate: ICV antisense against Galpha-i2 causes ependymal ciliary
   stasis and ventricular dilatation in rats. Note the authors deliberately do not use the word
   hydrocephalus: "Since the intracranial pressure was not assessed in this study, we call the
   condition ventricular dilatation instead of hydrocephalus in this text."

   *** THE EFFECT IS TARGET-DRIVEN, NOT CHEMISTRY-DRIVEN. THIS IS UNAMBIGUOUS. ***
   The study carries three concurrent control arms at identical route, dose and schedule: saline
   (n = 22), nonsense ODN (n = 17) and mismatch ODN (n = 5) against antisense (n = 27). The
   mismatch ODN is described in the Methods as "a more stringent control, maintaining equal base
   composition to the antisense molecule but with eight mismatches". Neither control ODN produced
   any ventricular dilatation in vivo or any change in ciliary beat frequency in vitro at the same
   exposure, while Galpha-i2 protein knockdown in ependymal cells was independently confirmed by
   confocal immunohistochemistry with two different antibodies. In addition, the dilatation was
   strictly unilateral and confined to the infused ventricle - the contralateral, 3rd and 4th
   ventricles in the same animals were unchanged - which is what a local pharmacological knockdown
   looks like and not what a systemic or chemistry-mediated toxicity looks like. And the in vitro
   time course argues the same way: unlike the directly ciliotoxic pneumolysin positive control,
   the AS-ODN effect "emerged gradually, after a delay", and cell morphology "appeared normal at
   the timepoint when ciliary stasis occurred", i.e. function was lost before structure.
   These four independent lines all point the same way. Filed as measurements TMP_hb_m23 and
   TMP_hb_m26 (the two chemistry-control rows) and TMP_hb_m18 (the within-animal contralateral
   control).

   *** TWO GENERALISATION LIMITS THAT MATTER AS MUCH AS THE MECHANISM VERDICT. ***
   (a) CHEMISTRY. The molecule is an UNMODIFIED PHOSPHODIESTER DNA 18-mer - the Methods say
       "unmodified 18-mer oligonucleotides" and describe RNase-free handling "to prevent
       degradation of unmodified oligonucleotides". Zero phosphorothioate linkages, no 2'
       modification. It shares essentially no chemistry with nusinersen, tofersen or tominersen.
   (b) EXPOSURE PROFILE. The dilatation required CONTINUOUS Alzet minipump infusion at 25 ug/day
       for 7 days. A SINGLE 20 ug ICV BOLUS "was without any effect (results not shown)" - the
       authors attribute this to CSF flow diluting a bolus below the effective concentration.
       Clinical intrathecal ASOs are given as intermittent boluses, not continuous infusions.
       Filed as TMP_hb_m22, flagged as a "results not shown" author assertion with no n and no
       statistics.
   Net: this paper supports "knocking down Galpha-i2 causes ventricular dilatation in rats". It
   does NOT support "intrathecal ASOs cause hydrocephalus". Sequences transcribed verbatim from
   the Methods for all three ODNs and stored on TMP_hb_5/6/7.

=== ITEM 4: WHAT THE MECHANISTIC LITERATURE CONTAINS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT ===
Searched PubMed via E-utilities with 18 distinct queries covering: oligonucleotide/ASO/siRNA x
ventricular volume, ventriculomegaly, ventricular dilatation, ventricular enlargement; x CSF
outflow, outflow resistance, CSF production, CSF absorption, CSF clearance, CSF dynamics, CSF
flow, CSF pressure, opening pressure; x ciliary beat, cilia beat, beat frequency; x ependymal /
ependyma; x choroid plexus (including with toxicity, vacuolation, degeneration, histopathology);
x intracranial pressure, papilledema; phosphorothioate x cilia/ciliary/ependymal; phosphorothioate
x ventricle/ventricular/hydrocephalus; intrathecal/ICV ASO x hydrocephalus; nusinersen x
hydrocephalus/ventriculomegaly/ventricular volume; tofersen/tominersen/BIIB067/IONIS-HTTRx x
hydrocephalus/ventriculomegaly/ventricular volume; organoid/iPSC x ependymal/choroid plexus/cilia
x oligonucleotide; aquaporin x antisense x hydrocephalus. Result counts recorded during the sweep;
candidate hits screened by title and abstract.

WHAT EXISTS (the complete list, as far as this sweep can establish):
  - Monkkonen 2007 (PMID 17430589) - the only study anywhere that measures EPENDYMAL CILIARY BEAT
    FREQUENCY after oligonucleotide exposure, and the only one that measures ventricular volume by
    MRI after ICV oligonucleotide in a healthy animal. Extracted in full here, 10 rows.
  - Korff 2026 (PMID 42018666) - hydrocephalus incidence scored in ASO-treated mice. 2 rows here.
  - Antonyan L, et al. "Prevention of hydrocephalus with a small oligonucleotide." Mol Ther 2026
    Feb;34(5):2944-2962. PMID 41612697. DOI 10.1016/j.ymthe.2026.01.034. ASOs targeting SETBP1
    prevented or significantly reduced hydrocephalus in a Schinzel-Giedion syndrome mouse model
    (>50% hydrocephalus untreated) and improved survival. ALREADY IN THE DATASET
    (extractions/hydrocephalus.json), so deliberately NOT duplicated here. Worth recording in this
    note because it is the strongest single piece of evidence against a general chemistry-driven
    hydrocephalus mechanism: an ICV/IT ASO made hydrocephalus BETTER, not worse. Its PMC deposit
    (PMC13154258) is embargoed until 2027-05-06.
  - Lan 2026 (PMID 42545100) - human CSF volume and glymphatic index before and after nusinersen.
    5 rows here.
  - Viscidi 2021 (PMID 33962637) and Groulx-Boivin 2024 (PMID 39308455) - disease background. 14
    rows here.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST, as far as this sweep can establish - and these gaps are findings, not
failures to search:
  - NO measurement of CSF OUTFLOW RESISTANCE after oligonucleotide exposure in any species. The
    seven hits on the CSF-outflow queries were unrelated (choroid plexus peptide biology, PK
    modelling, siRNA-nanoparticle hydrocephalus therapeutics). This is a complete blank.
  - NO measurement of CHOROID PLEXUS SECRETORY FUNCTION or blood-CSF barrier integrity after
    oligonucleotide exposure. The choroid-plexus queries returned 95 hits, essentially all about
    using the choroid plexus as a delivery route or target, none about oligonucleotide toxicity to
    it. The one hydrocephalus-relevant hit (PMID 40640139, Nat Commun 2025) uses SPAK siRNA in
    lipid nanoparticles to TREAT hydrocephalus by reducing CSF hypersecretion - again a
    therapeutic, and again in the opposite direction to a toxicity signal.
  - NO ependymal cilia beat frequency measurement after any MODERN oligonucleotide chemistry.
    The only CBF data in the entire field is Monkkonen's unmodified phosphodiester DNA. The
    "phosphorothioate x cilia/ciliary/ependymal" query returned 5 hits, ALL unrelated (rabbit
    ocular iontophoresis and older unrelated work). There is no phosphorothioate-gapmer, 2'-MOE,
    cEt, LNA or siRNA ciliary study at all.
  - NO human iPSC, organoid or other in vitro human-based ependymal or choroid-plexus model
    exposed to an oligonucleotide. The organoid/iPSC x ependymal/choroid-plexus/cilia x
    oligonucleotide query returned 9 hits, none of them such a study. This is the single largest
    gap relative to what NCATS says it wants (human in vitro systems), and it is a gap in the
    world, not in this dataset.
  - NO ventricular volume, ventriculomegaly or hydrocephalus study for tofersen, tominersen,
    BIIB067 or IONIS-HTTRx: that query returned ZERO hits. The only clinical
    ASO-hydrocephalus report outside SMA is the Huntington's case report already in the dataset
    (PMID 33125799, Mov Disord 2021).
  - NO non-human-primate intrathecal ASO study with a ventricular or ependymal endpoint. The
    IT/ICV x oligonucleotide x toxicity x ventricle/ependymal query returned 3 hits, none of which
    is one (the closest, PMID 39882764, is a 41-week cynomolgus IT study reporting spinal cord
    findings and is already in the nonclinical lane).
  So: the verification round's conclusion that this literature is close to empty is CORRECT, and
  it is now precisely characterised. The whole mechanistic case rests on ONE 2007 rat paper using a
  chemistry no clinical ASO uses, delivered by a schedule no clinical ASO uses, whose own controls
  show the effect is target-specific.
